Additional Public Prosecutor for R1 & R2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ORDER

This petition has been filed challenging the proceedings initiated by the respondent against the petitioner under Sections 420 of IPC and Section 4 of the Prize Chit and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978.

entities.text: Prize Chit and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2.The grounds raised by the counsel for the petitioners are all factual in nature and it requires appreciation of evidence and this Court cannot decide the same in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code.

The facts of this case and grounds raised in the quash petition do not fall within the parameters laid down by the Apex Court in State of Haryana and others v. Bhajanlal and others [(1992) Suppl (1) SCC 335].

entities.text: State of Haryana and others v. Bhajanlal and others [(1992) Suppl (1) SCC 335]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is left open to the petitioners to raise all the grounds before the Court below and the same shall be considered on its own merits and in accordance with law.
This Court is not inclined to interfere with the proceedings pending before the Court below.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
3.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the trial has already commenced and the case is posted on 21.03.2024 for examination of LW-106 to LW-120.
This is yet another reason as to why this Court is not inclined to entertain this petition.
4.The learned counsel for the petitioners requested this Court to dispense with the presence of the petitioners.

Taking into consideration, the facts and circumstances of the case, the presence of the petitioners is dispensed with and he shall be represented by a counsel, who shall cross examine the witnesses on the same day, they are examined in Chief.

The petitioners shall be present before the Court below at the time of questioning under Section 313 Cr.P.C., at the time of passing of the final judgement and as and when required by the Court below.

The petitioners shall appear before the concerned Court and execute a bond under Section 88 Cr.P.C..
5.Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition is disposed of with a direction to the Court below to complete the proceedings in C.C.No.6 of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2019, as expeditiously as possible.
The trial shall be conducted on a day to day basis in accordance with the guidelines given by Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in Vinod Kumar Vs State of Punjab [2015 (1) MLJ (Crl) 288 SC].

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Vs State of Punjab [2015 (1) MLJ (Crl) 288 SC]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the petitioners adopts any dilatory tactics, it is open to the trial Court to insist upon the presence of the petitioners and remand him to custody as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH VS. SHAMBHU NATH SINGH (JT 2001 (4) SC 3191).
